# Private Credit, Software, and Energy

Report 184 | Published 2026-03-15 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2026-3-15/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/184.json)

Private credit, banks and energy stress.

This report updates the Iran view and makes useful distinctions between bank deposits and patient investment capital. The central banking conclusion has partial independent support, but exposure ratios are not sufficient stress tests and the treatment of undrawn credit as not yet risky is incorrect. Adobe’s reported business growth is stronger evidence than its claimed cheapness.

**Coverage:** Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.

## Claims

### 184-C01

**Dollar debts create compulsory crisis demand.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | dollar-debt-financial-channel |
| Source blocks | 9, 10, 11 |
| Thesis family | dollar-debt-financial-channel |

Fixed dollar obligations require dollar settlement unless renegotiated. Falling revenues can force borrowers to acquire dollars or liquidate assets. This bounded mechanism does not imply that the exchange rate always rises, since other flows can dominate.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Deductive assessment:**

- Dollar obligation remains payable
- Borrower lacks sufficient dollar cash
- No refinancing or renegotiation

The borrower must convert resources into dollars or default. Aggregate exchange-rate effects additionally depend on other demand and supply.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.

### 184-C02

**Costlier energy squeezes other spending.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | energy-income-squeeze |
| Source blocks | 13, 25 |
| Thesis family | energy-income-squeeze |

For a household or firm with a fixed nominal budget, higher expenditure on an unchanged energy quantity leaves less for other uses. Producer income, borrowing, fiscal transfers and substitution prevent this partial-equilibrium identity from proving an equal aggregate-demand loss.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Deductive assessment:**

- Budget fixed
- Energy quantity unchanged

Non-energy budget equals total budget less price times energy quantity; increasing energy price reduces that residual.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |

Reserve-management operations verify the response framework. Access, collateral eligibility and stigma constrain facilities, and central-bank liquidity cannot cure an insolvent borrower. This supports a backstop, not coverage of every financial problem.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Early experience with reserve management purchases](https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/speeches/2026/per260326) | New York Fed | 2026-03-26 | Verified in the audit

The Desk purchased about $40 billion monthly ahead of expected April tax flows. The objective was maintaining ample reserves.

Bank funding risks remained moderate. Some semi-liquid private-credit funds capped redemptions; bank credit lines were among their funding resources. Traditional closed funds differ materially from redeemable vehicles.

### 184-C14

**Investor capital absorbs losses before bank lenders.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Bank claim is senior to fund equity |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | private-credit-loss-waterfall |
| Source blocks | 94, 109, 113, 125 |
| Thesis family | private-credit-loss-waterfall |

The priority mechanism holds for a solvent fund’s ordinary senior secured borrowing with adequate equity/subordination. It does not guarantee collateral valuation, enforceability or liquidity under stress, nor apply uniformly to every nonbank structure.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Deductive assessment:**

- Single asset pool
- Senior bank debt legally enforceable
- Equity junior
- No off-balance-sheet senior claims

If asset value falls but remains above senior debt, residual equity bears the decline. Senior principal becomes impaired once asset value falls below its claim.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.
